title_en: Yin Ruijun v. Yan Likui — dispute over right to health and bodily integrity
ruling_gist_en: When a victim of a criminal case sustains physical injury due to the criminal act and does not initiate a civil action attached to the criminal proceedings, but instead separately files a civil tort action, the question of whether disability compensation falls within the scope of material loss is not expressly provided for in the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC and its judicial interpretations. Where a victim of a criminal case becomes disabled due to the criminal act, his or her future life and work will inevitably be affected, resulting in reduced labor capacity, increased living costs, and consequently an indirect reduction of material income. Therefore, disability compensation should be considered as falling within the category of material loss and should be compensated.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over right to health; dispute over right to bodily integrity; second instance; intermediate people's court; Anhui Province; natural person; Tort Liability Law; Criminal Procedure Law; whether disability compensation constitutes material loss; determination of lost wages; compensation for mental distress; partial support; intentional injury; separation of criminal and civil proceedings; disability assessment
full_text_en:
Yin Ruijun v. Yan Likui — Dispute over Health and Personal Rights

Ruling Summary

Where a victim of a criminal act suffers bodily injury and does not file an incidental civil action in the criminal proceedings but instead separately files a civil tort action, the Criminal Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations do not clearly stipulate whether disability compensation falls within the scope of material losses. Since criminal acts that cause disability to the victim inevitably affect the victim's future life and work, resulting in reduced labor capacity, increased living costs, and consequently a de facto reduction in material income, disability compensation should be categorized as material loss and be compensable.

Plaintiff: Yin Ruijun, male, 62 years old, residing in Tianjia'an District, Huainan City, Anhui Province.

Defendant: Yan Likui, male, 58 years old, residing in Tianjia'an District, Huainan City, Anhui Province.

Plaintiff Yin Ruijin instituted an action with the Tianjia'an District People's Court of Huainan, Anhui Province, due to a dispute with Defendant Yan Likui over health and personal rights.

Plaintiff's Allegations: At approximately 5:00 p.m. on November 26, 2012, Yin Ruijun quarreled with Defendant Yan Likui's wife in the community vegetable plot. To retaliate, Yan Likui stabbed Yin Ruijun with a knife, causing injury. Yin Ruijun was sent to the hospital for treatment on the same day. Yan Likui intentionally injured Yin Ruijun and should bear compensation liability. The claims sought: 1. Yan Likui to compensate Yin Ruijun for medical expenses, appraisal fees for the degree of personal injury, photocopying fees, hospital meal subsidies, transportation expenses, and clothing and shoe losses, totaling RMB 13,047.27; after appraisal, additional claims were made for lost wages of RMB 18,283.87, nutritional fees of RMB 3,330, nursing fees of RMB 15,234.25, moral damages of RMB 8,000, and disability compensation of RMB 46,228. 2. Yan Likui to bear the litigation costs.

Defendant's Defense: 1. This case arose from a physical altercation between neighbors and was not retaliation; 2. Yan Likui has already received criminal punishment and should only bear direct economic losses; disability compensation and moral damages should not be borne; 3. Plaintiff Yin Ruijun had no lost wages; 4. Yin Ruijun's hospitalization was essentially an empty bed holding for treatment purposes only, and the appraisal materials cannot be used as valid evidence.

Basic Facts Found by the Court at First Instance (Tianjia'an District People's Court):

Plaintiff Yin Ruijun and Defendant Yan Likui both resided in Laolongyan Dongquan Village, Tianjia'an District, Huainan City. At approximately 5:00 p.m. on November 26, 2012, the parties quarreled and fought over a community vegetable plot issue. Yan Likui stabbed Yin Ruijun with a knife, causing minor injuries. Yin Ruijun was subsequently sent to the hospital for treatment. Yan Likui was later sentenced to one year and three months of fixed-term imprisonment for the crime of intentional injury. On August 25, 2014, Yin Ruijun separately filed a civil lawsuit and applied for appraisal of disability grade, period of lost work, nursing period, nutritional period, and subsequent treatment expenses. The appraisal opinion issued by the appraisal institution lawfully commissioned by the court determined that: Yin Ruijun's injury was equivalent to a Class 10 disability under road traffic accident standards; the period of lost work was 180 days; the nursing period was 150 days; the nutritional period was 111 days; since Yin Ruijun currently has no specific subsequent treatment items, the appraisal for subsequent treatment expenses was not accepted.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the identity cards of Plaintiff Yin Ruijun and Defendant Yan Likui, medical records and related payment invoices, the appraisal opinion, and the criminal judgment, which are sufficient to establish the facts.

Judgment at First Instance (Tianjia'an District People's Court, Huainan, Anhui Province):

The main issue in this case was: How should the compensation items and amounts to be borne by Defendant Yan Likui to Plaintiff Yin Ruijun be determined? Citizens or legal persons who infringe upon another's personal rights through fault shall bear civil liability. This dispute has already been handled through criminal proceedings. Yan Likui intentionally injured Yin Ruijun and shall bear corresponding civil compensation liability. Furthermore, according to the Criminal Procedure Law and its relevant judicial interpretations, for personal injury caused by a criminal act to the victim, compensation shall be paid for reasonable expenses incurred for treatment and rehabilitation, such as medical expenses, nursing fees, and transportation fees, as well as income reduced due to lost work. If the victim is disabled, expenses such as the costs of assistive devices for daily living due to disability shall also be compensated. If the victim or their legal representative or close relative did not file an incidental civil action during the criminal proceedings but separately files a civil lawsuit, the people's court may conduct mediation or render a judgment based on the material loss situation. Therefore, regarding Yin Ruijun's various claims: Medical expenses of RMB 8,737.27 — the reasonable portion of RMB 7,171.39 was supported; hospital meal subsidies of RMB 2,160 — Yin Ruijun was hospitalized three times for a total of 111 days, calculated at the standard of RMB 30 per day — Yin Ruijun's claim did not exceed the legal standard and was supported; transportation expenses of RMB 1,080 — because Yin Ruijun did not provide relevant supporting receipts, RMB 555 was discretionarily supported; nutritional fees of RMB 3,330 — based on the appraisal determining a nutritional period of 111 days, calculated at RMB 30 per day, Yin Ruijun's claim complied with legal provisions and was supported; nursing fees of RMB 15,234.25 — based on the appraisal determining a nursing period of 150 days, because Yin Ruijun did not provide the income status of the nursing personnel, calculated by reference to the average annual wage of RMB 37,074 per person per year for the residential service and other service industries in the province for the previous year, the amount of nursing fees was determined to be RMB 15,235.89, and Yin Ruijun's claim did not exceed the legal standard and should be supported. Yin Ruijun's claims for medical record photocopying fees and clothing and shoe losses did not comply with legal provisions and were not supported; the claims for appraisal fees and lost wages lacked sufficient basis and were not supported; the claims for disability compensation and moral damages, because they do not fall within the scope of material losses caused by criminal acts under Chinese law, were not supported. In summary, the compensation amount Yin Ruijun should receive in this case was RMB 27,340.64.

Accordingly, the Tianjia'an District People's Court of Huainan, Anhui Province, rendered a judgment on June 10, 2015, based on Articles 98 and 106 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC*, Articles 4, 5, and 6(1) of the *Tort Liability Law of the PRC*, Articles 99 and 101 of the *Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC*, Articles 155 and 164 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC*, Article 64(1) of the *Civil Procedure Law of the PRC*, and Article 2 of the *Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings*, ordering: 1. Defendant Yan Likui shall, within fifteen days after this judgment takes effect, pay Plaintiff Yin Ruijun a lump sum compensation of RMB 7,171.39 for medical expenses, RMB 2,160 for hospital meal subsidies, RMB 555 for transportation expenses, RMB 2,220 for nutritional fees, and RMB 15,234.25 for nursing fees, totaling RMB 27,340.64; 2. All other claims of Plaintiff Yin Ruijun are dismissed. Litigation costs of RMB 2,380: Yin Ruijun to bear RMB 1,896, Yan Likui to bear RMB 484.

Yin Ruijun appealed against the first-instance judgment to the Huainan Intermediate People's Court, arguing: 1. The first-instance finding that Appellant Yin Ruijun had no lost wages was unclear in fact. 2. The first-instance court erred in holding that Yin Ruijun's claims for moral damages and disability compensation did not fall within the scope of material losses caused by criminal acts under the Criminal Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations and should not be supported; compensation should be granted. This case should not apply the Criminal Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations. In summary, the appellant requested the second-instance court to revoke the original judgment and order the Appellee Yan Likui to pay Yin Ruijun lost wages of RMB 18,283.87, disability compensation of RMB 46,228, and moral damages of RMB 8,000, totaling RMB 72,511.87; and to bear the litigation costs of both instances.

Appellee Yan Likui argued: 1. The first-instance decision not to support lost wages was correct; 2. Disability compensation and moral damages do not fall within the scope of material losses caused by criminal acts and should not be compensated. The appellee requested the second-instance court to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

In the second-instance hearing, neither Appellant Yin Ruijun nor Appellee Yan Likui submitted new evidence.

The Huainan Intermediate People's Court, upon second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

Reasoning of the Second Instance (Huainan Intermediate People's Court, Anhui Province):

The issues in the second instance were: Whether Appellee Yan Likui should bear compensation liability for Appellant Yin Ruijun's claimed lost wages, disability compensation, and moral damages. 1. Regarding lost wages: Yin Ruijun is a retired employee. For a retired employee claiming lost wages, they should produce evidence such as a labor contract or employment contract, payroll records, or an employer's lost-wage certificate. However, Yin Ruijun only submitted a business license and an attendance record marked from June to September 2012, which is a short period. This evidence is insufficient to support Yin Ruijun's claim for lost wages; therefore, the claim for lost wages was not supported. 2. Regarding moral damages: Yan Likui has already been sentenced to one year and three months of fixed-term imprisonment for the criminal act of injuring Yin Ruijun. This criminal punishment serves as a form of moral solace for Yin Ruijun. Moreover, moral damages do not fall within the scope of material losses. Therefore, Yin Ruijun's claim for moral damages is not supported. 3. Regarding disability compensation: First, based on the facts of this case and relevant legal provisions, Yan Likui's intentional injury caused Yin Ruijun to suffer a Class 10 disability. Articles 4 and 16 of the *Tort Liability Law of the PRC* respectively provide that where a tortfeasor bears administrative or criminal liability for the same act, it does not affect the assumption of tort liability in accordance with the law; where a tort causes disability to the victim, the tortfeasor shall compensate the victim for disability compensation. Based on these facts and legal provisions, Yin Ruijun's claim for disability compensation has factual and legal basis. Second, from the perspective of fairness, the harm caused by a criminal act to the victim may be even greater than that caused by a purely civil tort. If disability compensation is not supported, the victim of a criminal act would receive less compensation, while the victim of a purely civil tort would receive relatively more compensation, which would be unfair to the victim. Supporting disability compensation better conforms to the principle of fairness. Third, considering the nature of disability compensation, where a tort causes disability to the victim, it inevitably affects the victim's future life and work, resulting in increased living costs or reduced labor capacity, thereby de facto reducing the victim's material income. Disability compensation should thus fall within the scope of material losses. In summary, Yin Ruijun's claim for disability compensation should be supported. The amount of disability compensation is calculated with reference to the 2013 per capita disposable income of urban residents in Anhui Province, combined with Yin Ruijun's disability grade. The amount of disability compensation is RMB 46,228 (RMB 23,114 per year × 20 years × 10%).

Additionally, the first-instance judgment calculated the amount of nutritional fees as RMB 3,330 based on the appraised nutritional period of 111 days at the standard of RMB 30 per day, but erroneously determined the amount of nutritional fees in the main text as RMB 2,220. This should be corrected; the amount of nutritional fees is RMB 3,330.

In summary, the findings of fact in the first-instance judgment were clear, but the application of law was partially erroneous, and the judgment should be amended.

Accordingly, the Huainan Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province, based on Articles 4, 6(1), and 16 of the *Tort Liability Law of the PRC*, Article 138(2) of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC*, Articles 17(1), 17(2), 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, and 25 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Personal Injury Compensation Cases*, and Article 170(1)(ii) of the *Civil Procedure Law of the PRC*, rendered the following judgment on January 7, 2016:

1. The civil judgment (2014) Tian Min Yi Chu Zi No. 01805 of the Tianjia'an District People's Court of Huainan, Anhui Province, is hereby vacated;

2. Appellee Yan Likui shall, within fifteen days after this judgment takes effect, pay Appellant Yin Ruijun a lump sum compensation of RMB 7,171.39 for medical expenses, RMB 2,160 for hospital meal subsidies, RMB 555 for transportation expenses, RMB 3,330 for nutritional fees, RMB 15,234.25 for nursing fees, and RMB 46,228 for disability compensation, totaling RMB 74,678.64;

3. All other claims of Appellant Yin Ruijun are dismissed.

Litigation costs of the first instance, RMB 2,380: Yin Ruijun to bear RMB 672, Yan Likui to bear RMB 1,708; litigation costs of the second instance, RMB 300: Yin Ruijun to bear RMB 109, Yan Likui to bear RMB 191.

This judgment is final.
